chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-Amraki ibn Ali — all of them from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the word of Allah the Exalted: 'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the parable of His light is as a niche' — that is Fatima (peace be upon her); 'in which is a lamp' — that is al-Hasan; 'the lamp is in a glass' — that is al-Husayn; 'the glass is as if it were a brilliant star' — Fatima is a brilliant star among the women of the people of this world; 'kindled from a blessed tree' — that is Ibrahim (peace be upon him); 'an olive tree, neither eastern nor western' — neither Jewish nor Christian; 'whose oil would almost glow' — knowledge almost bursts forth from her; 'even if no fire had touched it — Light upon Light' — an Imam from her after an Imam; 'Allah guides to His Light whomever He wills' — Allah guides to the Imams whomever He wills; 'and Allah strikes examples for the people.'

I said: (What about) 'Or like utter darknesses?' He said: The first one and his companion — 'waves cover him' — the third one; 'above him waves, darknesses' — the second one — 'one above another' — Muawiya and the strife of Banu Umayya. When the believer extends his hand in the darkness of their trial, he can barely see it. And whoever Allah does not give light — an Imam from the progeny of Fatima (peace be upon her) — he has no light of an Imam on the Day of Resurrection.

And he said regarding His word: 'their light runs before them and on their right hands' — the Imams of the believers, on the Day of Resurrection, will run before the believers and on their right, until they lodge them in the dwellings of the people of Paradise.

key_terms.شَجَرَة مُبَارَكَة: Blessed tree — identified with Ibrahim (AS) and his pure lineage
key_terms.فِتَن بَنِي أُمَيَّة: Trials of Banu Umayya — the political strife and oppression of the Umayyad dynasty
key_terms.كَوْكَب دُرِّيّ: Brilliant/radiant star — an epithet for Fatima (AS) among all women
key_terms.مِشْكَاة: Niche — identified with Fatima (AS) in this tafsir
key_terms.نُورٌ عَلَى نُورٍ: Light upon light — interpreted as the succession of Imams from Fatima's lineage

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of Ayat al-Nur (Quran 24:35) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a detailed esoteric commentary on Quran 24:35 (Ayat al-Nur), identifying each metaphorical element with members of Ahl al-Bayt: Fatima as the niche, Hasan as the lamp, Husayn as the glass, and Ibrahim as the blessed olive tree, with knowledge bursting forth from Fatima and each Imam succeeding another as 'light upon light.' He then interprets the opposing 'darkness' verse (24:40) as the first three Caliphs, Muawiya, and the trials of Banu Umayya, concluding that whoever lacks an Imam from Fatima's progeny will have no light on Judgment Day. The hadith culminates with an interpretation of Quran 57:12, identifying the 'light running before believers' as the Imams who guide the faithful to Paradise.
